display.title: Bedikas Chametz: Searching the House for Chametz
display.summary_short: A Yiddish lesson for children on Bedikas Chametz: cleaning ahead of time, hiding ten pieces, the brachah, searching every corner with a candle and saying Kol Chamira.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children, following the Seder Hanhagos shel Pesach page of the Haggadah. Before Pesach all chametz must leave the house. Cleaning starts weeks earlier: chametz is eaten only in the kitchen or dining room, sefarim are kept off the chametz table, and toys are checked for crumbs, since cookies turn up under pillows and in pockets. On the night before Erev Pesach one takes a feather, a wooden spoon, a candle and a bag, and first hides ten hard pieces of chametz around the house, like a game of hide and seek. After the brachah Al Biur Chametz one may not talk about other things until the search is done. The whole family searches every room and corner by candlelight, finds all ten pieces, ties up the bag and puts it somewhere safe from little children and mice. The chametz for breakfast should also be put away, so that a missing tenth piece does not mean searching all over again. Finally one says Kol Chamira, declaring any unseen chametz ownerless, like the dust of the earth, and goes to sleep early to be ready for Erev Pesach.
display.lesson: We search for chametz carefully and completely, and nullify whatever we could not find, so that no chametz is ours on Pesach.

relations.note: Same teaching appears in 'hg1a' at about 2:40-16:40; this file is a tighter edit of that recording.
